note: upstream v0.22.0 (candidate from packaging/upstream, compatibility suite passed)

patches.why: Windows: `gateway start` from a scheduled task or VBS spawns a breakaway, detached gateway so a job object cannot kill it.
patches.upstream: not upstream; drop when upstream gateway_windows handles breakaway

patches.why: Windows: Bot Chat DMs no longer write into a poisoned temp directory.

Under the PM layout, restarts and cron bot-chat delivery honor HERMES_BIN (the bare store Python cannot import Hermes once the child env drops its path); native-crash stacks go to logs/faulthandler.log.

The payload's venv is built on the release PC and its pyvenv.cfg names that PC's folder, so its launchers (venv\Scripts\python.exe, which Hermes puts first on PATH) exit 103 on every other PC. When that folder is gone, children get the interpreter itself first on PATH instead.
patches.upstream: half upstream since v0.21.6: a sealed payload's venv Scripts no longer go on PATH on Windows. Still ours: the interpreter's own folder goes on PATH, so a child's bare `python` is the bundled one. `.next` is that remainder written for v0.22.0's activate_dependencies.

patches.why: Microsoft changed the token its free Edge speech service requires (2026-10-13); edge-tts 7.2.7 gets 403 and every Edge voice reply fails. 7.3.1 (same author, reviewed: the new token and a progress helper, no new endpoints) works. Moves the pin in pyproject.toml and uv.lock.
patches.upstream: not upstream; drop when upstream pins edge-tts 7.3.1 or later

patches.why: Local models: `local_runtime.models_dir` puts models, their companions and download partials in a folder the owner chooses (a model is 16 GB or more; Hermes keeps them under its own root, and its partials on that drive, so a finished file couldn't be renamed into a folder on another drive). `local_runtime.catalog_refresh: false` keeps the catalog the release shipped instead of upstream main's newest, unsigned list.
